editorial:
Imagine spending your whole day making the trashiest TV shows possible just to get people to watch. That is exactly where you find Nikola, a guy who has basically given up on having a moral compass. He spends his time filming vulgar hidden camera pranks and low-brow reality TV. But things get interesting when he meets a young girl whose mom is pushing her way too hard to become a famous star. As Nikola starts mentoring her, you can see him slowly waking up to how empty his own life has become. It is a funny but sad look at how we treat fame and people like products for a screen.

What really works here is how the movie keeps you guessing. You start to wonder if Nikola is actually the one being pranked by a giant show he cannot see. The acting feels real and the pacing keeps you moving along without feeling slow. While some parts might feel a bit too cynical for some, it is a great ride if you like stories about the fake side of Hollywood. You should definitely try streaming this in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the details, or you could rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night with friends.
endingExplained: In the end, the lines between reality and the show totally blur. Nikola realizes that his attempt to help the girl was just another part of a larger game. The big twist reveals that he was indeed the target of a hidden camera setup all along. He ends up facing the same emptiness he used to create for others, leaving you to wonder if anyone in the TV world is ever actually being honest.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves movies that poke fun at reality TV and fame.
